# Independent code review iteration

Scope: independent full pass over the `octomation/go-module` template at `efe80d1` (2023-12-28): sample Go API and tests, Makefile/Taskfile, module and toolchain metadata, documentation, reusable/local Actions, delivery and maintenance workflows. Existing reviews were not used as input; overlap with prior reviews is intentional independent corroboration. Offline issue and roadmap dumps were excluded.

Validation: `GOFLAGS=-mod=readonly go test -race ./...`, `GOFLAGS=-mod=readonly go vet ./...`, and `go test -cover ./...` passed on Go 1.26.5; default coverage is 5.6% because the network path is integration-tagged. The first test attempt was inconclusive due a transient module-proxy socket error and passed on retry without source changes.

Severity: **Crit** / **High** / **Med** / **Low** / **Nit**.
Class: `correctness` · `security` · `concurrency` · `perf` · `api` · `idiom` · `modern` · `test` · `build` · `docs`.

## 1. Commit messages are interpolated directly into a privileged shell script

The composite action embeds `${{ github.event.head_commit.message }}`, `${{ github.event.inputs.reason }}`, and a workflow name directly inside a `run: |` heredoc. GitHub expands expressions before Bash parses the script. A message containing shell syntax, command substitution, or the heredoc delimiter can therefore alter the generated program. The action receives the Slack webhook and is used by CI and deployment jobs, so this is an executable injection surface, not only malformed output.

**Fix.** Pass event data through `env` and append it to `$GITHUB_OUTPUT` with a random delimiter or a small action/script that treats input as data. Never place `github.*.message`, `reason`, `name`, `title`, or refs inside inline shell. Reference: [GitHub script-injection guidance](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/concepts/security/script-injections).

## 2. Module-only dependency updates bypass CI

Both event blocks use the literal `go.{mod,sum}` path. GitHub path globs do not perform shell brace expansion, so neither `go.mod` nor `go.sum` matches. A Dependabot root-module update can avoid linting, tests, generation, and vulnerability checks even though the repository advertises those as template guarantees.

**Fix.** List `go.mod` and `go.sum` separately in `pull_request.paths` and `push.paths`; include `tools/go.mod`, `tools/go.sum`, and docs lockfiles in their respective workflows. Reference: [GitHub path pattern syntax](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/workflows-and-actions/workflow-syntax#patterns-to-match-file-paths).

## 3. Documentation delivery can deploy a commit that never passed its trigger

The Pages and Cloudflare workflows run on `workflow_run`, but checkout has no `ref`. For that event GitHub's default `GITHUB_SHA`/ref points at the default branch, while the payload separately exposes `workflow_run.head_sha`. If main advances after CI run A succeeds and before delivery A starts, checkout can build newer commit B and publish it even if B is failing or untested.

**Fix.** For `workflow_run`, checkout `ref: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.head_sha }}` and use the same SHA for provenance. Alternatively build docs in CI and promote the immutable artifact from the successful run.

## 4. A boolean health probe panics on routine network failures

`Ping(ctx, m) bool` calls `PanicOnErr` for request construction, transport, and XML decoding. DNS failures, cancellation, non-HTML responses, and transient TLS errors are normal health-check outcomes, yet the API crashes the caller instead of returning false or an error. It also uses `http.DefaultClient`, does not check HTTP status, and accepts `*Module` nil only to panic on dereference.

**Fix.** Return `error` (or `(bool, error)`), validate `m`, use `http.NewRequestWithContext`, check a 2xx status, cap the response body, and inject a client with a timeout for testability. Reserve panic for an explicit Must helper.

## 5. CI coverage depends on a live external vanity endpoint

The coverage target runs tests with the `integration` tag, so `TestIntegration` calls `Ping(context.Background(), NewModule())` against `https://go.octolab.org/?go-get=1`. There is no context deadline and transport failures panic. Availability, DNS, certificates, or changed HTML outside the repository can make release-gating coverage fail or hang.

**Fix.** Unit-test the parser with `httptest.Server` and an injected client. Keep a live smoke test separate, give it a deadline, and do not make it the sole producer of the coverage artifact.

## 6. The supposed compile check actually executes the full test suite

`go-check` uses `-test.run=^$(uuidgen)`, but `uuidgen` is not a Make variable and expands to an empty string. The resulting regexp is `^`, which matches every test. CI therefore runs the suite in the "fast source check" and then runs it again in the explicit test step; in repositories derived from this template that may duplicate slow or stateful tests.

**Fix.** Use an impossible literal such as `-run='^$'` for compile-only validation, or remove the redundant target and let the real test job be the only execution path.

## 7. A new-project template defaults to an unsupported Go era

The generated module declares Go 1.11 and CI spends twelve lanes on 1.11-1.21 plus floating latest. Tooling is pinned to Go 1.21 and 2023-era forks. This teaches new projects to optimize for versions long outside the Go support window, prevents modern language/library use, and multiplies CI cost without a consumer policy.

**Fix.** Choose an explicit support floor appropriate for newly generated code (normally the current or previous supported release), test only that floor plus current, and separate a legacy branch/template if old consumers genuinely require Go 1.11.

## 8. The integration command installs the wrong module

The README tells users to run `go get go.octolab.org@latest`, while this module is `go.octolab.org/template/module`. That command fetches the unrelated root `go.octolab.org` module and does not demonstrate consuming the generated module.

**Fix.** Show `go get go.octolab.org/template/module@latest` in this template, and ensure repository initialization rewrites both module paths and docs examples atomically.

## 9. The fuzz target passes a package path as the fuzz regexp

`go-fuzzing-test` invokes `go test -fuzz $(PACKAGES)`. The first package token is consumed as the required regexp argument to `-fuzz`, rather than selected as a package; multi-package modules then have ambiguous trailing arguments. There are no fuzz targets here, so the command cannot provide the promised validation.

**Fix.** Require an explicit `FUZZ` regexp and call `go test ./... -fuzz="$(FUZZ)" -fuzztime=...`, or delete the target until a real fuzz test exists.
